fields.meta_title: Rental Application Form: Build It Online Free | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A rental application form that collects the screening fee and reads pay stubs, with every applicant saved to a table you own.
fields.h1: Build a Rental Application Form That Arrives Complete
fields.hero_description: A rental application form gives a landlord what the decision rests on. Describe your rental, and Emergent builds the form and a table of every applicant.
fields.features_heading: Every Answer the Rental Decision Needs
fields.features_subheading: A paper rent application form arrives with a check clipped to it. These six features turn it into a file you can decide on.
fields.feature_1:
The questions a landlord decides on

Asks for current and past addresses with each landlord's phone number, then the employer and monthly pay. Every person moving in is listed, with signed consent to a credit check.
fields.feature_2:
The screening fee paid at submit

Collects the screening fee at the last step through the payment processor you connect, then emails an itemized receipt. Set the amount per property to match local fee caps.
fields.feature_3:
Pay stubs read into monthly income

Reads each uploaded pay stub or offer letter into the employer and gross pay for the period, then works out monthly income. A stub it cannot read clearly goes to a person.
fields.feature_4:
A separate link for each co-signer

Sends every adult on the application and any guarantor their own link. Each one enters their own income and signs for themselves, and the file shows who has not finished yet.
fields.feature_5:
One table holding every applicant

Saves each application as a row in a database you own, showing the unit and move-in date beside income against rent. Filter by property, or open any row to see the uploads.
fields.feature_6:
Your app as code in your repo

Exports the full source to your GitHub repo. A developer can connect it to your screening service or property software through an API, or you can describe the change in a prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
Fee paid and pay stubs attached in one sitting

Dana rents out one side of her duplex and links the application from her listing. Applicants finish it on a phone: past addresses with landlord numbers, then monthly pay and two recent pay stubs. The $40 fee goes through Stripe at submit, and each application reaches her table with its stubs attached.
fields.tab_content_2:
Income under three times rent goes to a person

Northwind Property Group posts one set of written criteria and applies it to every applicant in the order they arrive. Each file shows monthly income beside the rent. Anyone under three times the rent is never declined by the form: a leasing agent reviews the file and can ask for savings statements or a guarantor.
fields.tab_content_3:
Household income measured against the limit for its size

Income-restricted units cap what a household can earn, and the cap rises with the number of people. The Cedar Grove application lists everyone moving in and each adult's yearly income, then adds them up. A household of three earning $60,000 sits under the $72,000 limit and moves to document review.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each guarantor signs from a separate link

Students at Elm Hall rarely earn what a lease asks for, and each application names a guarantor. That guarantor gets an email with a separate link to enter their own employer and income, then sign as guarantor. The file stays incomplete until the signature is in, and the leasing office sees who is still waiting.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Rental Application Form
fields.howto_description: Decide what earns a yes before you draft any questions. The form and every decision letter follow from that.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Check the fee rules for the unit
fields.howto_step_1_des: Set the minimum income and the credit standard that earn an approval, and put them in writing before the listing goes up. Review applications first come, first served. Each decision then has a reason you can point to later.
fields.howto_step_2_des: The Fair Housing Act bars decisions based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status or disability. Drop any question that touches them, like country of birth or plans for children. Ask how many people will live there instead.
fields.howto_step_3_des: New York caps the screening fee at $20 or the actual cost, whichever is less. California sets its own cap, raises it each year with inflation and requires an itemized receipt. Look up the rule for every state and city you rent in.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste your criteria and fee into the prompt and name the uploads you need, such as pay stubs or a photo ID. Emergent builds the form with a table for the applicants. Reword any question later by asking for the change in plain English.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the consent checkbox and your screening disclosure ahead of the fee step. Run the credit and background check through the screening service you already use, connected by its API, and its report lands on the applicant's row.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Confirm income with the employer, then call the previous landlord about late payments and the notice they gave. Compare what you hear with the written criteria before you decide, and record the outcome on the applicant's row.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Federal law requires an adverse action notice when anything in a screening report shaped a denial. It names the agency that supplied the report and tells the applicant they can get a free copy within 60 days.
